group.passage:
All species of plants have their own ways to survive. They multiply or reproduce mainly through pollination. Pollination commonly occurs through the wind blowing, through insects carrying the pollen from plant to plant or through self-pollination. A primitive plant called a cycad is pollinated by insects named thrips and the way by which it attracts bugs is very special and unique.
Known as “living fossils” because of their primitive structure, cycads have been around since some 290 to 250 million years ago. Cycads’ seeds are exposed on the surface rather than enclosed. A cycad’s main trunk is usually underground, with its leaves sticking up above ground situated around a single cone. The color of the cone changes from greenish to yellow as it matures. The scales of the cone start to open during pollination, when they spread to leave tiny spaces in between the scales.
Scientists previously believed that cycads were pollinated by wind blowing pollen from male cones to female cones. But later, the theory was overturned because the space was too small to successfully pollinate. Then they discovered the thrips, a real cycad pollinator. This is how it works: cycads reproduce through the pollination carried out by the thrips activity. Cycads have a pollination period, during which male cones have the unique ability to raise their temperatures at midnight each day to emit a substantial odor known as beta-myrcene. When increasing to toxic level, the odor is lethal to the thrips and thus drives them away from the male cones with pollen stuck to their bodies. As the dawn approaches, the plants cool down and emit much lower levels of beta-myrcene, which again attracts the thrips and the pollen they carry away back to the plants, especially to the female cones. In the process, the thrips effectively remove pollen from the male cones and leave it in the female cones and the successful pollination is completed.
Scientists believe that plants have evolved by producing chemical defenses in order to drive away animals that would eat them. Over centuries, cycads have refined the functions they are capable of to become a sustainable species. That is why cycads have existed over a timeline of more than 250 million years.

options.B: The cycad attracts thrips during pollination.
options.C: The cycad becomes warm during maturation.

questions.stem: Based on the passage, which of the following statements is true?

options.A: The seeds of a cycad are hidden in the leaves to avoid thrips.
options.B: Thrips usually go from male cycads to female ones to pollinate.
options.C: The simple structure of the cycad has helped itself survive attacks.
options.D: The smell from beta-myrcene attracts thrips to help with pollination.
